multifactorial — The patient's symptoms (polydipsia, polyuria, polyphagia, weight loss, hyperglycemia, glucosuria, ketonuria) are classic signs of diabetes mellitus, likely type 1 given the recent onset and presence of ketones in urine (though serum ketones were negative at bedside testing). While other forms of diabetes exist, the presentation strongly suggests an autoimmune destruction of pancreatic beta cells leading to insulin deficiency.. Diabetes mellitus type 1 is typically caused by autoimmune destruction of pancreatic beta cells, leading to insulin deficiency. This process is considered multifactorial because it involves a combination of genetic susceptibility (multiple genes conferring increased risk) and environmental triggers (like viral infections) that initiate the autoimmune response. No single gene defect or chromosomal abnormality is sufficient to cause type 1 diabetes; rather, multiple genetic variants interact with environmental factors to cross a threshold for disease development
